**Stage1 typed-`try … else` parity fix completed against the newest Stage0 seed (2026-09-26):** the remaining Stage0/Stage1 acceptance disagreement was the exact error-handling fixture where `extern read_file(path: u8&) -> cstr[file_text] error[IoError]` was used as `try read_file(path) else "".cast[u8&]`. Stage0 correctly rejected the fallback (`try fallback expects cstr[file_text], got u8&`), while Stage1 previously accepted it.

Root cause and invariant:

- The parser represents a value recovery as `Expr.Refinement(fallback, guarded)`, with the fallback first. The cast syntax `"".cast[u8&]` is an `Expr.Index(Expr.Field(..., "cast"), target)`; it is not an `Expr.Call` around an indexed callee. The old Stage1 check therefore never recovered the cast target.
- `Decl.Extern` intentionally keeps compact ABI metadata, and the general `Symbol.return_type` path must not be filled with the first token of a compound extern return: for `mutable heap void&?`, that token is `mutable`, and publishing it globally caused unrelated runtime calls to become incorrectly typed. The corrected checker leaves normal extern symbol inference untouched and pairs the named extern symbol’s declaration line with the parser’s existing `__extern_return` annotation only for this narrow fallback check.
- The checker now handles direct indexed casts, parenthesized targets, reference targets, interned return `TypeId`s for ordinary functions, and compact extern return names. It emits the appended `TryFallbackTypeMismatch` diagnostic without weakening the runtime pointer checker or the separate runtime-only zeroed-reference rule.

Verification performed from `/Users/torarinvikbjarko/Documents/Coding Projects/Elisa Projects/Elisa-compiler` using the fresh Stage1 product:

- `DEVELOPER_DIR=/Library/Developer/CommandLineTools EMSDK_PYTHON=/opt/homebrew/bin/python3 ELISA_STAGE1_SEED_MAX_RSS_KB=8388608 bash scripts/elisac_stage1.sh --seed` completed and rebuilt both `bin/elisac-stage1` and `build/runtime/elisacore_runtime.o`.
- The exact reproducer now reports one diagnostic at the fallback line: `try fallback expects cstr, got u8&`; the acceptance contract intentionally compares error class, while preserving the known compact-extern spelling limitation. No physics source, Marble asset, tolerance, or browser artifact changed.
- `ELISA_ACCEPT_JOBS=4 bash test/parity/semantic_acceptance_diff.sh` passes `581/581` Stage0 end-to-end cases.
- `bash test/parity/zeroed_reference_safety_smoke.sh`, `bash test/parity/try_fallback_void_smoke.sh`, and `git diff --check` pass.
- `bash test/parity/driver_acceptance_smoke.sh` passes the with-stdlib profile with `0` disagreements and the bare profile within its existing ratchet (`2` reject-gaps versus `6` allowed).

Required continuation: keep the product freshness guard before every parity run; do not copy compact extern head tokens into general return-type inference; if byte-for-byte diagnostic wording for `cstr[file_text]` becomes a requirement, extend the parser’s extern side metadata to preserve the full return spelling and test that change independently. This compiler fix removes the Stage1 acceptance blocker; the separate Marble hard replay and browser-physics parity work remain open.

The compiler-level cause of the three WASM parity-smoke failures was isolated.
Stage0 treats WASI as POSIX-ish because the WASM runtime uses the
POSIX-shaped `mmap`/`munmap`/`malloc`/`free`/`mem*`/`write` seam. Stage1's
`src/backend/codegen_static_if.elisa` incorrectly changed
`ELISA_TARGET_OS_POSIX` to false for WASM, removing the POSIX platform
declarations and causing 21 concurrency functions to be declined during every
Stage1 WASM runtime build. The compiler fix keeps the POSIX predicate true for
WASI and is included in the product above. This is a compiler fix, not a
port-side workaround.

The remaining `wasm32_sview_strlen` failure was a parity-fixture defect exposed
after that compiler fix: the fixture declared the Elisa-only nullable
`sview(cstr?, ...)` helper as an extern C function with `cstr`, which cannot
describe the optional payload ABI and produced the expected wasm signature
mismatch. The fixture now calls the public C-compatible
`ctx_string_view(cstr, ...)` wrapper, separately exercises target-sized
`strlen`, and checks a generic `i32`-to-`i64` zero extension instead of relying
on an internal generated temporary name. No compiler ABI rule was weakened.

Focused verification after these changes passed:

```text
python3 -m unittest discover -s nw-core/test -p stage1_fresh_test.py

wasm32_sview_strlen_smoke.sh     PASS (stage0 == stage1 == 63)
wasm32_for_bounds_width_smoke.sh PASS (stage0 == stage1 == 6)
```

numerical trace or the cross-rasterizer pixel-policy decision; both remain

**Diagnostic trace-schema compatibility correction (2026-09-28):**
the phase synchronizer now treats newly added engine arrays as optional when
reading an older retained WASM trace. A historical trace cannot contain an
array introduced after it was captured, so the synchronizer skips only that
missing field and continues copying every field that exists on both sides;
size mismatches for present fields still fail loudly. The same rule is used
for event-level synchronization and before-step synchronization, and the
delta report compares only fields present in the retained snapshot. This is
a diagnostic-harness compatibility fix only; it changes no runtime artifact,
physics source, tolerances, or acceptance policy.

**Stage1 view-element address lowering fixed and regression-locked (2026-09-28):**
the remaining compiler-side reject gap in affine_move_projection.neg.elisa
was isolated to the Stage1 backend, not to the Elisa fixture. Stage0 accepted
peek(&xs[0]) when xs: view[Handle], while Stage1 declined the enclosing
element_read body because its place resolver could read view[T][i] but had
no address path for the same element. The fix adds one shared
emit_view_index_address implementation in
Elisa-compiler/src/backend/codegen_convert.elisa. It loads the {data, len}
view aggregate, applies the existing count bounds guard, and emits an
element-stride GEP. codegen_place.elisa now dispatches that helper for both
named local views and nested view-valued fields, so &xs[i] and
&state.tokens[i] use the same ABI and safety rule as value reads.

The backend IR smoke suite now contains a focused view_element_address
assertion for the emitted view.elem.ptr GEP. Against the newest stable Stage1
seed at compiler commit

bea037dbddc0dc2302051a7fd8fe5ee000cc9ea889fbf5a6fb85b87036de0952, the

### Rejected Marble `mji_dot6` FMA candidate — 2026-09-30

Native arm64 disassembly localized the first event-0 public-state divergence to
the inline six-component RNE projection (`mji_dot6`) used by `mj_rne`: native
code contracts the multiply/add sequence into fused instructions, while the
WebAssembly build emitted separate `f64.mul`/`f64.add` operations. A disposable
MuJoCo candidate therefore wrapped only `mji_dot6` in an Emscripten-side `fma`
path, without changing the production WASM artifact or the accepted tolerance.

The candidate was built from MuJoCo commit `13827e9ee56f097f57acf69ae52b078f9839682d`
and replayed through the strict rung-16/seed-0 source parity trace. It produced
the same first numeric breach at event 196 (`value[10]` delta
`1.0094403890548165e-7`), the same 111,546 scalar exceedances, the same maximum
delta `9.997690068805735`, and the same timeout terminal state as the production
artifact. The event-0 diagnostic also remained split at `qfrc_bias`: native
`1.5407439555097887e-33` versus WASM `0`. Consequently the candidate is rejected;
its temporary patch hunk was removed from `marble-wasm-parity.patch` and neither
candidate binary was promoted. The production MuJoCo hashes remain
`mujoco.js=d9ef82762e323c7a549d4eafaf35395f07aef7265e840e6dc0f9c40460847357`
and `mujoco.wasm=2ce3a5933d7174b442c052e691d74e9f3a34075c95ce8f9b44efddbad1146f38`.

The result means that a source-level call to the C `fma` symbol is not evidence
of native-equivalent fused rounding in this WebAssembly toolchain. The next
investigation must inspect the generated `fma` implementation and prove its
numeric semantics before any further physics change is considered. No tolerance
increase, source-oracle change, or visual exception is justified by this test.

## Emscripten explicit-FMA lowering probe — 2026-09-30

The next Marble diagnostic required verifying whether the checked-in
`__EMSCRIPTEN__` `fma()` calls actually provide a native-style single-rounding
operation. A disposable standalone probe was built with Emscripten 6.0.10 from
`/opt/homebrew/bin/emcc`, both with its normal `-O3` lowering and with
`-ffp-contract=off`. The probe exported an explicit `fma(a, b, c)` function and
an ordinary `a * b + c` function.

Two witnesses were evaluated in the generated WASM and compared with the host
AppleClang/libm result: a normal cancellation case
`a=0.85614055058838223`, `b=0.85757312403591035`,
`c=-0.73420312658190334`, where ordinary evaluation rounded to zero while the
explicit FMA returned bit pattern `0xbc8af0732f42f3b8`; and a subnormal case
`a=-3.7185939400817586e-268`, `b=-1.5293578594780632e-17`,
`c=-4.0178574646740566e-285`, where ordinary evaluation returned
`0x04cfc574a6190cc4` and explicit FMA returned `0x04cfc574a6190cc3`.
The WASM explicit-FMA outputs matched the host fused results in both cases under
both compiler flag variants. The disassembly also confirms the expected software
fallback implementation; the absence of a WebAssembly fused instruction is not
itself evidence of incorrect `fma` semantics.

This closes the generic-FMA-runtime hypothesis. It does not validate any
particular MuJoCo operation-family rewrite: the current synchronized event-195
trace still localizes the first fresh public difference to the free-joint
`mji_crossMotion` component-5 outputs, and the previously tested component-5
candidate failed the complete hard replay. No production MuJoCo source, vendor
asset, compiler flag, tolerance, or browser artifact changed. The next Marble
candidate must therefore be an independently justified operation-family or
runtime-semantics explanation and must pass the unchanged strict replay,
contact-topology, terminal-result, and broad trajectory gates.

The Stage0 compiler issue fixed during this continuation was an ownership
analyzer defect. A packed enum match creates a refined variant view and binds a
payload such as `taken` from a field such as `job.thread`; the analyzer previously
tracked the binder under the shadow view instead of the original affine path.
An early move/return through the binder therefore left the original field marked
live and rejected valid code. The fix records match-pattern projections, follows
`PackedVariantViewType.AliasOf` back to the true scrutinee, and propagates
consumption only through `*ast.MatchBindPattern` aliases. Ordinary immutable
locals retain independent ownership roots. The focused five-case regression set
and the full `go test ./test/semantic -count=1` package pass, and the port's
Stage0 fast compiler package tier is green.

The gate intentionally skipped the slow `stage0 test-full`, Stage1 self-host
fixpoint, and Stage1 semantic differential tiers. The full compiler `go test
./...` attempt passed the modified semantic, backend, parser, lexer, interpreter,
EASM, frontend, and test packages but timed out in the aggregate `elisacore/src`
runtime harness after ten minutes while other builds were active. That timeout
is recorded as unverified infrastructure coverage, not converted into a false
pass.

The latest checked-in browser MuJoCo runtime was rebuilt from the pinned

The strict source replay remains **failed and open**. On the deterministic
7,601-event rung-16 / run-seed-0 / board-seed-827307999 replay, source and
WASM both time out, but the first strict state-tolerance breach is event 216,

over-tolerance values and later contact/friction-state divergence; matching
the terminal timeout does not make the trajectories equivalent.

New identical-input probes show that the split is not explained solely by
different game inputs or a large single-step physics error. At startup,
`qfrc_bias` already differs by only `1.5407439555097887e-33`. When the native
engine is reset from each captured WASM `mj_step1` input around event 216,
the first substep's solver outputs differ at near-roundoff scale (for
example, `qacc` by `7.11e-15`); the largest recorded solver-output delta in
the second substep is `2.27e-13`, with `qpos` within `1.12e-16`. Across the
unsynchronized replay, accumulated orientation and
angular-velocity deltas grow before event 216, then a contact/friction active
set threshold amplifies them into a materially different trajectory. This is
strong evidence for accumulated floating-point sensitivity, but the exact
upstream arithmetic source of the full-run drift is not yet resolved.

Two additional Emscripten arithmetic candidates were explicitly rejected and
removed from the production patch: an FMA-first `mji_crossMotion` hunk moved
the first breach to event 195 and increased exceedances to 113,948; an
explicit nested-FMA `mju_mulInertVec` candidate also moved the first breach
to event 195 (110,770 exceedances). Keep the retained cross-force candidate;
do not reintroduce either hunk without a full controlled improvement. The
artifacts currently in the repository are the cross-force candidate, not
either rejected build.

A follow-up isolated only the three `mji_crossMotion` correction-pair FMAs
(components 3–5), leaving its primary cross terms unfused. This matched the
native `cdof_dot` outputs for the captured event-216 operands exactly, but the
full hard replay reproduced the same regression as the broader cross-motion
candidate: first breach event 195, delta `4.771133337300171e-7`, and 113,948
over-tolerance values. Reject this variant too. Exact local kernel matching
does not prove that changing that kernel improves the long trajectory; do not
continue exploring cross-motion-only arithmetic as a presumed fix.

Next, continue from the saved synchronized phase traces in
`/private/tmp/nw-mj-solver-baseline-diagnostic/traces/`. Localize the earliest
per-substep output difference from identical inputs at event 0 and in the
pre-contact interval leading to event 216, distinguishing live physics
outputs from stale/uninitialized diagnostic buffers. Any candidate must pass
the strict unsynchronized 7,601-event/contact replay, the broad 162-scenario
trajectory suite, the 80-board result matrix, and a strict held-input win.
Never relax tolerances or claim Marble parity complete based only on board,
session, single-step, or terminal-result tests.

**Phase-diagnostic lifetime filtering and rejected `mji_cross` z-component FMA (2026-10-01):** corrected the diagnostic harness before using retained phase traces to make arithmetic decisions. Marble resolves `mjJAC_AUTO` to a dense Jacobian (`nv=18`), so sparse-index arrays (`efc_J_colind`, `efc_J_rowadr`, `efc_J_rownnz`, and `efc_J_rowsuper`) are inactive storage, not comparable outputs. The phase comparator now filters those fields for a dense model, excludes solver/island arrays until their producer phase, and avoids reconstructing elliptic-cone metrics before `efc_state` and `efc_force` are live. An opt-in `NW_MARBLE_DIAGNOSTIC_PHASE_UPDATES=1` report classifies differences as newly produced, updated-existing, or carried; this is diagnostic-only and does not change parity assertions. Re-running the saved event-0 trace confirms `checkPos`, `checkVel`, `kinematics`, `comPos`, and `fwdPosition` have no live array mismatch after synchronization; the first newly produced residual remains `qfrc_bias` at `probe_rneBias`, magnitude `1.5407439555097887e-33`. This removes previously misleading allocator garbage and carried solver state from the investigation.

At event 216, exact per-substep input synchronization exposes a separate point-Jacobian split at `phase.comPos`: contact 0 / side 1 / `jacp[39]` differs by `6.776263578034403e-21`, and contact 2 / side 1 / `jacp[51:53]` differs by up to `3.3881317890172014e-21`. Reconstructed operands are identical; the changed coordinate is the third output of `mji_cross`, `a[0]*b[1] - a[1]*b[0]`, followed by the existing translational-component addition in `mj_jac`. For the recorded event-216 operands, explicitly fusing that cross term reproduces the native values exactly.

The lifecycle-aware solver-phase comparison places these roundoff differences without showing a contact-state branch split in the synchronized samples. At event 0/substep 0, after the RNE residual, `qfrc_bias` differs by `1.5407439555097887e-33` and `qacc` by `4.9679927381240586e-27`. At substep 1, `solver_stats` is first newly produced with max delta `7.558002607596976e-16`; solver inputs/outputs such as `efc_b` and `qacc` are updated-existing. At substep 2, `efc_force` first becomes live, while all three elliptic contact state values remain 0 on both engines. At synchronized event 216, the `comPos`/`probe_comVel` differences identified at that event precede the solve; substep 0 `fwdConstraint` has max `qacc` delta `7.105427357601002e-15`, and substep 1 reaches `efc_AR` delta `3.637978807091713e-12`. The reconstructed elliptic contact states still agree (all 0) in every synchronized substep examined at events 0 and 216. Thus these probes show accumulating numeric differences entering/updating the solve, but do not establish a mismatched contact-cone classification as the cause; the full unsynchronized replay's later contact-topology divergence remains a downstream symptom.

Tested this as an isolated candidate in a detached worktree at the pinned MuJoCo 3.12.0 commit, applying the maintained parity patch plus only an Emscripten-specific `mji_cross` `res[2] = fma(a[0], b[1], -a[1]*b[0])` operation. Emscripten 6.0.10 built the candidate successfully. The candidate phase trace removes all event-216 `comPos` point-Jacobian array differences, confirming the local hypothesis, but it does **not** improve end-to-end parity: on the same rung-16 / run-seed-0 / board-seed-827307999 replay, the first numeric tolerance breach moves earlier from retained event 216 to event 195, marble 0 / value 10, with delta `1.1375819641834539e-7` against `1e-7`. The diagnostic continuation completes all 7,601 events with the expected timeout and records 102 contact-set mismatches (first event 461, last event 1966). Reject this candidate; do not add its hunk to `marble-wasm-parity.patch` or promote its artifact. Exact local kernel matching is not sufficient evidence for a global physics correction. The retained production JS/WASM hashes remain `c91c0ae68e13721960ab5769852bd44d9a21bab60224c62806a09345c57dd04d` and `56a96b2306917e677beb5781be70e315856e65c2e35cde208aec00bc5cf4c1f8`.

Next use the retained source-faithful traces to connect (without re-running known local experiments) the already localized event-0 `mju_mulInertVec` component-1 rounding residual, the event-216 `cdof_dot` / free-joint cross-motion residual, and the first live constraint-solver divergence. These are MuJoCo C/WASM backend arithmetic differences on synchronized inputs, not evidence of an Elisa Marble scene-logic defect; any proposed compiler/runtime policy or engine-source change must predict effects at all three boundaries. Do not revisit the rejected `mji_cross` z-component or previously rejected `mji_crossMotion` FMA variants without a new causal explanation. Preserve the sparse/lifecycle-aware diagnostic classification. Any new candidate must be replayed unsynchronized across all 7,601 events and evaluated on both numeric tolerances and contact topology before broader gates or promotion.

### Marble exact-input constraint-solver audit — 2026-10-01

Inspected the pinned MuJoCo 3.12.0 source at commit
`13827e9ee56f097f57acf69ae52b078f9839682d` to connect the live phase deltas
to their consumers. In `src/engine/engine_core_smooth.c`, `mj_comVel` forms
`cdof_dot` with `mji_crossMotion`; `mj_rne` then uses
`cacc = cacc_parent + cdof_dot*qvel`, forms body forces using
`mju_mulInertVec` and `mji_crossForce`, and projects those forces onto `cdof`
to produce `qfrc_bias`. The synchronized traces show this live path at both
ends of the replay: at event 0/substep 0 the first new mismatch is
`qfrc_bias=1.5407439555097887e-33`; at event 216/substep 0,
`cdof_dot`/`free_joint_cross_motion` first differ by up to
`1.734723475976807e-18`, followed by a new `qfrc_bias` mismatch up to
`2.2973191744977036e-22`. The event-216 `qacc_smooth` mismatch is at most
`7.407502677679815e-16`.

The separate geometry path is now source-mapped too. At event 216/substep 1,
`fwdPosition` produces only three live array differences: three entries of
contact 0 / side 0 `jacp` (maximum `8.673617379884035e-19`), three entries of
`efc_J` (same maximum), and 19 entries of `efc_AR` (maximum
`3.637978807091713e-12`). The pinned source builds the point Jacobian in
`mj_jac`; `mj_projectConstraint` builds `Y` from `efc_J` and the factored mass
matrix, then `mj_makeAR` forms `efc_AR = Y*Y' + diag(R)`. The phase snapshot
shows the mass/factorization and other position-stage arrays equal here, so
the observed `efc_J`/`efc_AR` deltas follow the contact-Jacobian residual,
rather than a change in model topology or Elisa task state.

Crucially, the retained exact-input probe at
`/private/tmp/nw-mj-solver-baseline-diagnostic/traces/event216-sync-fwdconstraint.log`
replaces native data with the recorded WASM `fwdAcceleration` snapshot just
before `mj_fwdConstraint`. The synchronizer verifies exact equality for all
captured non-output engine arrays and contact fields; only outputs that
`mj_fwdConstraint` itself overwrites are excluded. Despite identical solve
inputs, the native wheel and WASM solver still produce different live
outputs: event 216/substep 0 `qacc` differs by up to `7.105427357601002e-15`
and `efc_force` by `4.336808689942018e-19`; substep 1 `qacc` differs by up to
`2.2737367544323206e-13` and `efc_force` by `2.7755575615628914e-17`. The
iteration-level `solver_stats` also differ at island 0 / iteration 3:
native reports `nactive=3, nchange=3`, WASM reports `0, 0`, while the final
elliptic contact-state values in the synchronized samples still agree. Thus
upstream RNE and Jacobian rounding contribute accumulated drift, but are not
the sole cause: a backend-level difference is reproduced inside the
constraint solve with its captured inputs held bit-identical.

This rules out the Stage1 compiler, Elisa Marble task logic, and browser input
as the cause of this strict-parity failure. The open fault is in the numerical
execution of the MuJoCo native-wheel versus Emscripten/WASM paths, including
solver iteration arithmetic/decisions; no single retained local FMA candidate
has passed the long replay. No production physics, compiler, thresholds, or
acceptance artifacts were changed in this audit. The temporary clamp hook
used while checking whether individual input families explained the output

### Stage1 compiler parity repairs — 2026-10-01

The compiler regression work resumed against the latest fetched Stage1 source,
`Elisa-compiler-remote-main` at `ce52ba2c5261ebced8f5dae9ca1e21f25db8f460`,
using the canonical Stage0 compiler at
`/Users/torarinvikbjarko/Documents/Coding Projects/Go projects/Elisa-core/compiler/bin/elisac`.
The compiler checkout already contained unrelated user changes; those were left
untouched. Headless macOS builds used
`DEVELOPER_DIR=/Library/Developer/CommandLineTools` to select the linker that can
read the installed macOS 27 SDK. The Stage1 product was reseeded after the final
source edit and passed its freshness guard; product SHA-256:
`7fde36a2fc09c5008c582ba0143aebdaf40ac2b7cf0cd38f4b98c5b30a07e49a`.

The true Stage1 semantic mismatch was region provenance loss. `new[r]` and
pointer-preserving `+`/`-` were not retained through the return-provenance
walk, so a value backed by a local region could pass Stage1 even though Stage0
rejected it. Stage1 now carries provenance for those pointer expressions and
returned local containers, while scalar comparisons intentionally carry none.
`region_scope_smoke.sh` covers the pointer-arithmetic escape and a structurally
similar scalar-comparison control. The affine-container fixture and diagnostic
gate now explicitly require both compilers to reject a moved local container
whose backing storage would outlive its region.

The native backend also had several distinct Stage0 parity gaps, repaired with
targeted regressions rather than blanket fallbacks:

* Value contexts now load through reference-valued fields and indexed elements,
  but preserve references when the expected result is itself a reference.
* Generic `push` resolution no longer masks a same-named monomorphic user method
  when no generic candidate matches.
* Darray literal spread now handles fixed arrays by evaluating/spilling the
  source once, then copying each element through the normal append path.
* A `darray[T]&` struct field is resolved as a pointer to the darray header:
  its pointer is loaded from the field slot before reads or mutation. Treating
  the slot as an inline header corrupted memory; the regression had segfaulted
  during `push` and now runs successfully.
* Reads through a reference-to-darray field use the header's item pointer and
  the actual element type/layout rather than interpreting the header as `T*`.

Final validation on this exact compiler source/product:

* `backend_native_smoke.sh`: **546/546** native compile-and-run/IR checks pass.
  This includes `darray_ref_field`, fixed-array spread, generic-name collision,
  and reference-value-context regressions. A first run overlapped a source edit
  and correctly encountered a stale Stage1 product plus a pre-fix emitter; it
  was discarded. The recorded 546/546 run started only after reseeding and
  rebuilding the emitter from the final source.
* `diagnostics_smoke.sh`: **698/698** fixture checks pass.
* `region_scope_smoke.sh`: pass, including the pointer escape, safe comparison,
  and 21 carrier-less annotation parity cases.
* `stage1_old_reference_ensure_smoke.sh`: pass (entry snapshots, success value,
  and exhaustion frame).
* `driver_acceptance_smoke.sh`: bare mode has **2** Stage0-accept/Stage1-reject
  cases against its existing allowance of 6; both are backend declines of a
  `for` statement in `loop_element_type.neg.elisa` and
  `param_structural_type.neg.elisa`. Both cases accept with the standard library
  included. The std-backed mode has **0 disagreements** against its zero-gap
  ratchet (0 accept-gaps, 0 reject-gaps). No ratchet was raised or expected
  result weakened.
* Stage0 and Stage1 freshness assertions and `git diff --check` pass.

When this compiler-parity checkpoint was first recorded, these fixes had not
yet been followed by a rebuild of `nw-core/build/nwcore.wasm` or its object.

#### Durable active-wheel cone-factor reproduction

Added `nw-core/test/marble_cone_update_oracle.py` and its regression tests. The
oracle loads the actual original MuJoCo wheel with `ctypes`, not a reconstructed
native engine, and replays `mju_cholFactor`, the original nested
`mju_addToScl` transformation, and `mju_cholUpdate` on captured operands. It
reports independent exact-input updates separately from sequential updates
whose previous result is propagated. Every report identifies the wheel path,
wheel SHA-256, trace path, trace SHA-256, event, substep, stage, difference
count, and first differing binary64 representation. No tolerance is applied.

The decoder validates finite numeric payloads, bounded integral dimensions,
contact-row ordering, full consumption, factor-chain continuity, and final
outputs before calling native code. `ncone` counts constraint rows, not
contacts. A rank update records its incoming factor, then `[k,nv]`, the
post-step vector, and post-step factor for each nonzero `x[k]`, followed by
the final factor/vector. Zero `x[k]` steps have no embedded record; parsing
must follow the captured vector as it evolves, not assume a fixed record count.
Sparse traces are not accepted by this dense decoder.

`nw-core/test/fixtures/marble_event216_cone_oracle.json`, SHA-256

#### Coherent scalar arithmetic model, still diagnostic only

The arm64 wheel's `mj_constraintUpdate_impl` instructions contract the
bottom-zone predicate, middle-zone denominator and projection, and scalar
cost accumulations. The diagnostic `wheel_order_update` reproduces those
operations together rather than applying the rejected projection-only hunk:

```text
bottom predicate: fma(mu, N, T)
middle denominator: (mu*mu) * fma(mu, mu, 1)
middle NmT: fma(-mu, T, N)
quadratic cost: fma((0.5*D)*jar, jar, previousCost)
middle cost: fma((0.5*Dm)*NmT, NmT, previousCost)
```

The existing separate force multiplications remain separate. The norm and
FMA routines are supplied explicitly. This model matches active-wheel
force/state/cost on all 24 captures and 1,024 deterministic synthetic states

into the browser runtime. The explicitly initialized Hessian extension below
is a separate constructed-input experiment.

Read-only inspection of the active original arm64 wheel's inlined
`_mj_solPrimal` at `0x1017a4..0x1019fc` confirms:

1. Normal initial coefficients use rounded products. DJj is a rounded D*jar
   product; tangent updates are sequential `fma(jar,DJj,q0)`,
   `fma(Jv,DJj,q1)`, `fma(Jv*D,Jv,q2)`.
2. U and V are separately rounded rescaled components. Tangent squared and
   cross sums use `fma(U,U,UU)`, `fma(U,V,UV)`, `fma(V,V,VV)` in row order.
   Fusing a different product or accumulating previously rounded products
   is not equivalent.
3. The Dm denominator has a rounded `mu*mu` factor multiplied by
   `fma(mu,mu,1)`. The additive factor is fused in the wheel. Half scaling
   occurs after the complete contact polynomial has been accumulated.

#### Recorder schema and safe decoding

Schema 1 repeats a 13-value header, followed by nefc+nf values:

~~~text
[1, evalOrdinal, preparationOrdinal, island, nv, nefc, ne, nf,
 alpha, cost, firstDerivative, secondDerivative, rawSecondDerivative]
R[nefc]
frictionloss[ne:ne+nf]  (serialized as a compact nf-value array)
~~~

Total width is 13+nefc+nf. Capacity is 300,000 doubles. Required initialized
bits remain 79. The preparation ordinal is reset to -1 at PrimalPointers and
assigned only after its complete preparation record is copied successfully.
Evaluation copies occur only after all output assignments and LSiter update.
It never reads uninitialized pre-search Jv or changes solver operands.

Gauss, Jaref, Jv, D, type/id/contact and active quad inputs come from the actual
associated preparation record. Do not recompute that quad before diagnosing
an evaluation: doing so mixes a preparation change into the supposed Eval
matched-input comparison. R and friction loss are added by this recorder.
Friction loss must start after equality rows, not at index zero. The corrected
C recorder and synthetic ne=1/nf=1 decoder/native-oracle tests cover this rule.

Reject missing/unknown schema, missing or truthy-not-false overflow/invalid
flags, nonfinite/non-numeric values, truncated/trailing values, noncontiguous
evaluation ordinals, nonexistent preparation IDs, mismatched dimensions,
negative impedance/loss, incomplete elliptic groups or inconsistent convexity
clamping. Bound native copy length before allocating/copying pointer buffers.
Do not invent a preparation ID or downgrade an invalid record to a pass.

#### Actual original private-function oracle

The original unmodified SDK-26 wheel has no public PrimalEval API. Calling an
SDK-27 rebuild with matching final outputs is insufficient for this boundary.
The test bridge therefore calls the verified original internal routine at
loaded-image offset 0x105808, anchored by public mju_dot at 0x10c504.

All guards are mandatory before constructing/calling the function pointer:

1. Darwin arm64 and exact authoritative wheel file SHA-256.
2. Double/pointer/int widths of 8/8/4 bytes; context/point sizes 632/32 bytes;
   contact structure size 584 bytes, mu offset 0xe8 and dim offset 0x210.

   ids 0x98; types 0xa0; Jaref 0x108; Jv 0x110; quad 0x140;
   Gauss 0x238; LSiter 0x264. These are specific to this verified binary.
4. dladdr must resolve the anchor to the same verified file and expected base.
5. Original entry bytes must equal ff8301d1ed33016deb2b026de923036d.
6. Whole bounded input validation, active quad widths, contact IDs and complete
   row grouping before allocation or native pointer access.
7. Owned buffers kept alive throughout the call; LSiter advances once; alpha
   is unchanged; every output is finite.

Unused partial-context padding is zero-initialized only to safely call this
known function, whose consumed fields were verified. Padding is not captured
solver scratch and is never parity evidence. Do not reuse guessed offsets
with another wheel/architecture or make this bridge a production requirement.
Rebuild or independently derive/guard a new oracle if the reference changes.

#### Outer packet schema and validity

Capture is enabled only around diagnostic mj_fwdConstraint. It is disabled
afterward. For each elliptic no-slip contact the actual solveQCQP function
copies its initialized local v before projection and immediately after it.
The actual costChange function writes its restoration flag at its existing
change > 1e-10 branch BEFORE replacing force and returning zero. Restoration
is not inferred from returned zero or from equal force vectors.

Capacity: 300,000 doubles. Header width 14, in order:

~~~text
index:  0       1        2       3          4    5        6
field:  schema  ordinal  island  iteration  row  contact  dim
index:  7      8         9       10         11        12          13
field:  route  validity  active  projected  restored  costChange  normal
~~~

Schema is 1. Route is the selected routine tangent dimension 2/3/5, or 0 on
the normal guard. Row is the global constraint row and dim is the full
contact dimension, not the number of tangents.

For n=dim-1, append mu[n], Ac[n*n], bc[n], oldForce[n], residual[n],
rawForce[n] when bit 1 is valid, postProjection[n] when bit 2 is valid,
and retainedForce[n] when bit 4 is valid. The normal guard uses mask 4,
route 0, active=-1 and projection 0: raw/projected arrays are not copied at all.
Ordinary solves use mask 7. Width is 14+n*n+7*n for an ordinary solve and
14+n*n+5*n for a normal guard. No uninitialized v or padding is transported.

Global schema/calls/overflow/invalid metadata are explicit. Captures reject
unsupported dimensions, invalid row/contact addresses, nonfinite values,
invalid masks and capacity overflow. The bounded Python decoder additionally
rejects booleans/coerced metadata, every truncation/trailing value, disordered
ordinals, inconsistent route/branch flags, nonpositive scaling and invalid
restoration/retained-force relationships. All metadata and complete operand
widths are validated BEFORE calling any original private routine.

Updated generated-play harness transports optional QCQP fields and refuses
overflow/invalid captures without changing ordinary production behavior.
It does not call fwdConstraint twice.

#### Marble hole-to-wall overlap fix and exact current verification — 2026-10-03

This checkpoint closes one specific, user-visible geometry defect: generated
pit/cup circles must not be covered by the rectangular wall strips. It does
not close the independent, stricter whole-game original-physics parity work
tracked above. The port must not be described as “identical to the original”
on the strength of board parity or this fix alone.

**Cause established from the pre-fix source.** Both hole placers used the
lower offset bound required to leave a legal far-side marble passage, and a
variety-based upper bound `half_corridor + 0.55 * hole_radius`. That upper
bound can place the circular pit beyond the corridor centreline by more than
the room available before the nearest wall. The wall strips themselves were
then emitted from the maze cell edges, so the hole and wall meshes occupied
the same footprint. This was a placement-geometry defect in the original
Python reference and the port's Elisa task implementation, not a Stage0 or
Stage1 compiler miscompile.

**Geometry invariant now enforced in both source implementations.** The
original source at
`/Users/torarinvikbjarko/Documents/Coding Projects/Python Projects/neural-workshop-enhanced/neural_workshop/marblemaze.py`
and the port at `nw-core/src/tasks/marblemaze.elisa` define
`HOLE_WALL_CLEARANCE = MARBLE_RADIUS * 0.20` (= 0.0015 m). For corridor
half-width `h`, pit radius `r`, hole margin `m`, and marble radius `b`, the
candidate absolute cross-corridor offset must be within
`[max(0, r + m + b - h), min(h - r - clearance, h + 0.55*r)]`.
Equivalently, the lower bound proves a marble-width passage on the far side;
the upper bound both keeps the whole circle in the corridor and guarantees a
positive wall gap. If the interval is empty, the layout is rejected instead
of silently placing an overlapping pit. To keep each requested hole layout
feasible while preserving this invariant, `Grade.slack` was raised on rungs
2–16 in both builders; rung 1 is unchanged. Keep the two parameter tables and
the Python/browser-facing board results in lockstep.

**Browser readout follows the corrected physical tray.** The corrected
corridor widths are 51, 50, 50, 47, 48, 45, 45, 43, 44, 41, 41, 39, 40, 37,
37, and 35 mm for levels 1–16. `nw-core/shells/web/marble-maze.js` now reports
those source-rounded values instead of its stale pre-clearance table. The
browser must continue to derive board surfaces and pits from the same
transported WASM geometry; do not add a browser-only hole relocation or hide
an intersection with draw-order changes.

**Regression is geometric, not a screenshot-only assertion.**
`nw-core/test/marble_board_abi_test.mjs` now constructs 16×20 deterministic
boards with seeds 0–17, 314159, and 1073741823. For every transported pit and
home cup, it computes the closest point on every transported axis-aligned
wall rectangle, subtracts the circle radius, and asserts the result is at
least 1.499 mm (1.5 mm target, 0.001 mm allowance for Float32 transport).
This checks pits and cup, every wall on each board, all 16 difficulty rungs,
and 320 seed/rung combinations. The current candidate measures 1.500 mm
minimum clearance at printed precision, with as many as 68 walls in a board.
The ABI malformed-payload guards remain part of this same test. Any future
change to wall widths, corridor sizes, pit radii, float encoding, or candidate
placement must retain this test and must not lower its clearance requirement.

The corrected geometry changes actual gameplay, so only two deterministic
held-input outcome labels changed in
`nw-core/test/marble_generated_play_session_test.mjs`: rung 2/runSeed 1 is now
a physical win (was loss), and rung 3/runSeed 17 is now a physical loss (was
win). The 80-case test still executes generated routes, physics, result
history, and disposal; do not weaken it to accommodate these updated
outcomes. The original Python reference and WASM board/MJCF comparison passes
80 cases over all 16 rungs and five established seeds. The candidate also

`nw-core/output/playwright/marble-wall-clearance-20261003/`; this server used

##### Resolved pit-to-wall overlap: cause, invariant, and exact acceptance rule

The visible defect came from invalid source board placement: pit centers were
chosen using a corridor bound that left no guaranteed separation from the wall
segments generated along maze-cell edges. The circles and the wall rectangles
could therefore intersect in the transported board. It was not a WebGL
z-fighting or draw-order artifact, and changing rendering order, hiding a wall,
or applying a browser-only pit offset would only conceal the defect while
leaving collision geometry wrong.

Both the original Python source and the Elisa port now use the same explicit
clearance constant, `HOLE_WALL_CLEARANCE = MARBLE_RADIUS * 0.20 = 0.0015 m`.
For corridor half-width `h`, pit radius `r`, hole edge margin `m`, and marble
radius `b`, the candidate absolute cross-corridor offset must be in
`[max(0, r + m + b - h), min(h - r - clearance, h + 0.55*r)]`. The first
bound retains the marble-width route on the far side of the pit. The second
bound keeps the complete pit circle inside the corridor and leaves at least
1.5 mm of clearance to the nearest corridor wall. Reject a layout if the
interval is empty; do not silently clamp to a value that violates either
constraint. Keep the source and port's rung parameters, rounding, board
transport, and geometry generation synchronized. Corrected source widths for
rungs 1–16 are 51, 50, 50, 47, 48, 45, 45, 43, 44, 41, 41, 39, 40, 37, 37,
and 35 mm; the browser readout must remain derived from the same current source
contract.

The durable regression is in `nw-core/test/marble_board_abi_test.mjs`: 16
difficulty rungs times 20 deterministic board seeds (0–17, 314159, and
1073741823), or 320 boards total. It decodes every transported pit and home
cup, computes closest-point distance to every axis-aligned wall rectangle,
subtracts the circle radius, and requires at least 1.499 mm after Float32
transport (1.500 mm target with only 0.001 mm representational allowance).
The check includes every wall on every board, as well as malformed-payload ABI
guards. The complete artifact gate reports a measured minimum of 1.500 mm at
printed precision, with up to 68 wall segments on a board. Do not replace this
with a screenshot-only assertion: the screenshot is supplementary proof of
rendering, whereas the numeric check proves non-overlap in the actual geometry.

Raising `Grade.slack` on rungs 2–16 was needed to make the requested hole
patterns feasible under the new hard bound; rung 1 stays unchanged. Because
these are gameplay geometry changes, retain the two reviewed deterministic
outcome updates in `nw-core/test/marble_generated_play_session_test.mjs`:
rung 2/runSeed 1 now wins instead of losing, and rung 3/runSeed 17 now loses
instead of winning. Do not force the former labels back or weaken the session
test; any further board change requires regenerating and reviewing those exact
outcomes against both source and port.

cast. This matches the newest runtime's libc declaration and the actual C ABI;
it does not weaken either compiler's escape checks. The exact latest pair now
passes `stats` 32/32 and `config` 342/342 cases on both generations.

#### Marble home-cup collar versus wall overlap (2026-10-04)

The physical pit/cup openings already have the 1.5 mm wall-clearance invariant,
but inspection of the actual generated scene found a second visual-only
overlap: the green home-cup collar was drawn at 1.34 times the hole radius, so
it extended underneath nearby wall strips even when the opening itself was
clear. On a 352-layout diagnostic sweep (16 rungs × 22 seeds), the nominal
collar crossed a wall on 154 boards. This did not change hole collision or
gameplay, but made the rendered cup look clipped by the maze wall.

The source reference UI, the port's native Python mesh builder, and the browser
WebGL renderer now use the same conservative rule. For each home cup, compute
the minimum Euclidean distance from its centre to every axis-aligned wall
rectangle, then cap the decorative outer radius at
`min(1.34 * holeRadius, nearestWallDistance - 1.5 mm)`. If that radius does not
exceed the unchanged hole radius, omit the decorative annulus. The opening,
board ABI, wall geometry, and physics remain untouched; ordinary fitted
collars retain their original 1.34× radius.

The promoted-production-WASM ABI regression now verifies both the existing
opening clearance and the renderer's actual collar-radius helper on all 320
established board layouts (16 rungs × 20 seeds, up to 68 walls). It passes with
1.500 mm minimum for both openings and emitted collars; 200 collars are
trimmed, including the rung-14/seed-0 overlap reproducer. The native mesh test
compares 560 meshes across 80 boards against the source `Builder`, using the
source's updated collar rule, and confirms 50 collars are trimmed with the
same 1.500 mm minimum. Browser renderer contracts pass. A live Playwright run
entered Marble Maze through the real menu, started the task with MuJoCo and
WebGL2, rendered the 3D tray, and reported no console errors. The retained
ordinary-run screenshot is
`nw-core/output/playwright/marble-collar-20261004/marble-maze-running.png`
(SHA-256
`b70c63baf16d2424f9b9f3c69971c866af8c81b698ceee79cc48b0ec5b2a75e4`). The
focused regression sweeps, rather than that non-deterministic screenshot,
cover the exact overlap layout. This closes the identified collar/wall
intersection path in these renderers; it does not close broader Marble visual
acceptance, approved pixel thresholds, or the remaining port plan.

#### Increase and prove Marble Maze pit-to-wall visual clearance — 2026-10-05

The user's report that holes appear to overlap the maze “walls” is a geometry
defect, not merely a renderer clipping artifact. The previous fix guaranteed a
1.5 mm minimum between each physical hole circle and a wall rectangle. That
removed literal overlap, but left a narrow visible gap which looked flush at
ordinary browser scale. The current milestone increases the minimum visible
clearance to 3.0 mm and applies it consistently to physical pits, the home
opening, and its decorative outer collar. Do not revert to the historical
1.5 mm rule; older sections above remain historical evidence tied to older
builds and should not be rewritten as if they used the new geometry.

**Geometry rule.** Let `H` be a transported hole center, `r` its applicable
radius, and `W=[x0,x1]×[y0,y1]` one transported axis-aligned wall rectangle.
Compute `dx=max(x0-H.x, 0, H.x-x1)` and
`dy=max(y0-H.y, 0, H.y-y1)`. The circle-to-rectangle clearance is
`hypot(dx,dy)-r`. Every emitted pit and home-hole circle must have clearance
at least `HOLE_WALL_CLEARANCE=0.40*MARBLE_RADIUS=0.003 m` against every wall
rectangle. Apply the same test to the outer home-cup collar radius, not only to
the physical hole radius. Float32 board-ABI tests permit at most 0.001 mm of
serialization error below the target; generated source geometry is checked
using the double-precision rule with its explicit `1e-12 m` comparison guard.
Do not test against an idealized cell grid when actual wall rectangles are
available: wall merges, edge strips, and board bounds make the emitted wall
geometry the relevant collision/visual geometry.

**Placement construction.** Candidate hole offsets must obey both the
far-side marble-passage lower bound and the nearest-wall upper bound. Reject a
placement/layout when its feasible interval is empty rather than weakening
the clearance. The effective upper bound is the smaller of the wall-safe
limit (`halfCorridor-holeRadius-clearance`) and the existing offset limit
(`halfCorridor+0.55*holeRadius`). Grade corridor slack on rungs 2–16 was
increased by 0.10 where required to retain a feasible hole interval; rung 1
remains unchanged. Preserve the original source's round-even corridor note
conversion, so browser labels stay in sync with generated board widths. Home
cup radius is now capped at the smaller of 40% of corridor width and 2.1
marble radii, but never below 1.5 marble radii. This specifically keeps the
largest radius-derived decorative collar at least 3 mm clear of nearby walls
on the narrowest grade. If future grade changes require another radius or
slack adjustment, first re-run source-vs-port board/MJCF parity and all grade
feasibility checks; do not patch only the visual mesh.

**Files and responsibilities.** The reference rules live in the original
Python checkout at
`/Users/torarinvikbjarko/Documents/Coding Projects/Python Projects/neural-workshop-enhanced/neural_workshop/marblemaze.py`.
The Elisa generator and wall-aware candidate/cup checks live in
`nw-core/src/tasks/marblemaze.elisa`. Browser and native presentation geometry
use `nw-core/shells/web/marble-maze-renderer.js` and
`nw-core/shells/python/marble_geometry.py`; both mirror the same 0.40R
minimum and trim only the decorative collar when necessary. Do not change the
physical opening merely to make a collar fit. The native/source UI is covered
by `nw-core/test/marble_ui_source_contract_test.mjs` and Python UI geometry
tests. The transported production layout is decoded and checked by
`nw-core/test/marble_board_abi_test.mjs`; this must examine every circle against
every serialized wall rectangle, including home-cup collar radius. Python/WASM
board and MJCF parity is guarded by `nw-core/test/marble_source_reference_diff.mjs`.

**Required verification, all completed for this checkpoint.**

the physics simulation retains a sub-millisecond remainder. On physical
settlement, however, the real `marbleTick()` path explicitly calls
`ACTION_SYNC_SETTLE_TIME` with `Math.round(marbleGame.elapsed * 1000)` before
reporting the physical result. An unsettled timeout feedback frame continues
to use the active-play floor. The metadata validator previously required the
floor for every phase, so it rejected a correct physical-loss capture by one
millisecond (controller 5667, physics 5666.666…). This is not a mismatch in
the compiler, physics solver, or promoted WASM. The validator now selects the
clock representation from the independently supplied source phase and
marble states: rounded milliseconds only for `won`/`lost`/`done` when every
marble is physically settled (`home` or `lost`); floor for running play and
unsettled timeout. Its focused fixtures cover a running 1/60-second frame
(controller16 ms, simulation17 ms), a settled loss at25/60 seconds
(controller417 ms), rejection of a stale 416 ms terminal controller value,
and timeout feedback. `python3 test/marble_browser_pair_metadata_test.py`
passes; the visual inventory's eight unit tests pass; the complete 24-pair
audit has no failures. This change is test/verification code only: no source
game code, compiler, generated artifact, runtime physics adapter, or WASM was
modified.

recorded source tree is
`e48688ca4edb0874d1f063844ec2e54e8faead200879aa4bbe5dd06fa7d65d5c`, and its
